methodology.metric: Action handler start to native revision/layout query acknowledgment, milliseconds
methodology.boundary: State update → React commit → wx.nextTick → identical native revision-marker geometry query callback
methodology.includes: Data generation, React reconciliation, host mutations, SDK scheduling and native layout-query bridge overhead

phases.commit: Handler start through React layout effect
phases.layout: React layout effect through the common native revision/layout query callback

methodology.scope: WeChat DevTools WebView + glass-easel; VPT DOM versus VPT template (the original Taro rendering architecture)

sampling.isolation: Fresh DevTools project window per case per block
sampling.transport: Localhost HTTP start handshake and completion callback outside the measured interval
sampling.recovery: Resume verifies identical builds and application sources. Every new context gets two warmups. All completed measurements, including those from interrupted contexts, enter the aggregates. Context interruptions and their observations are recorded.

methodology.aggregation: Median and nearest-rank p95; geometric mean of template/DOM median ratios; no outlier removal
methodology.validation: The timed common query verifies current revision ID and positive marker height. Every completed iteration also checks all native row IDs in order, row height, count, and selected class outside the timer.
methodology.limitations: Results rank these two renderers for keyed workloads in the recorded WeChat DevTools WebView environment. The metric includes SDK query/scheduling latency; device presentation and CPU tracing are separate measurements.
